nodes.label: Startup Read Policy
nodes.rationale: Agents must read a fixed ordered document set and only task-specific active docs afterwards, to avoid bulk-loading reference archives and to keep each rule in one canonical document.

nodes.label: Task Read Matrix
nodes.rationale: Maps each task area to the minimal set of active documents so agents read only what the current task requires instead of bulk-loading all contracts.

nodes.label: SOCD Last Input Wins
nodes.rationale: TOMAK resolves simultaneous opposite direction keys with Last Input Wins because fighting-game (Street Fighter 6, Tekken 8) keyboard/leverless players expect the most recent input to take priority; users are warned to check tournament rules.

nodes.label: Anti-Ghosting (KKUK Held-Key Refresh)
nodes.rationale: Not a physical matrix change: it periodically re-reports held key state for users (e.g. MapleStory kkuk-board players) who care about long held-key repeat feel; SOCD-assigned keys are excluded from this correction.

nodes.label: ERA VIA Keycode Quick Reference
nodes.rationale: User-facing list of QMK keycodes suitable for VIA input boxes; prefers older/compatible spellings (e.g. KC_MS_DOWN over MS_DOWN) because VIA lags behind current QMK keycode renames.

nodes.label: VIA TAPDANCE Keycode Entry
nodes.rationale: VIA CONFIGURE > TAPDANCE takes On Tap / On Hold / On Double Tap / Tap+Hold keycodes (e.g. KC_ESC, MO(1), KC_CAPS); the TD key must then be placed from the KEYMAP tab's CUSTOM area to take effect.

nodes.label: Non-volatile Memory Data Repositories
nodes.rationale: The nvm layer exists so the underlying data persistence mechanism is abstracted away from upper QMK code: per-system nvm_<<system>>.h headers expose value-based APIs (structs/unions) to owner systems, and all raw-field conversion happens inside provider-specific nvm_<<system>>.c implementations.

nodes.label: NVM Provider
nodes.rationale: Each provider is a child directory (e.g. eeprom) containing concrete nvm_<<system>>.c implementations of the upper nvm_<<system>>.h APIs. Systems that cannot persist on a provider must ship stub implementations that ignore writes and return sane defaults.

nodes.label: Split Port Safety
nodes.rationale: The inter-half USB-C connector is not a USB data port. On affected Tomak PCBs the D+/RX line carries a single-wire half-duplex serial line and firmware leaves D-/TX an input, so a normal USB-C to USB-C cable connecting D- to D- cannot drive the GP0/TX line against the other half. Firmware cannot fully protect against plugging the inter-half port into a PC or other USB host.

nodes.label: Single-Wire Split Link (460800 baud)
nodes.rationale: The two halves talk over one wire at 460800 baud. Both halves run one identical firmware image and are flashed together; a pair left on two different versions is not a supported configuration.

nodes.label: USB Session Ownership Without VBUS Sensing
nodes.rationale: Which half owns the USB session is decided by QMK's bounded USB-active detection at boot, not by sampling a VBUS pin. The firmware refuses a VBUS-pin role selection at build time, because raw VBUS sampling can race host enumeration and drop USB during master selection.
nodes.norm_label: usb session ownership without vbus sensing

nodes.label: Tomak Bootloader Entry
nodes.rationale: Three routes into the bootloader: bootmagic on the top-left key of the half being plugged in, a physical RESET/GND double short or a BOOT/GND short at plug-in, and the QK_BOOT keycode where the keymap places it.
